entries.defect: The published now-section can be empty or incomplete while `batch-in-flight --status` proves several active points; no current guard compares the full active-point set to the numbered now-cards, and open `feat/*` branches alone are not evidence of active work.

The numbered membership of “Woran ich gerade arbeite” is projected from the authoritative structured in-flight declaration alone while title/body prose remains human-authored; undeclared `feat/*` branches add nothing, and unreadable or contradictory source data is unresolved rather than interpreted as zero active work.

Board reconciliation keeps exactly one numbered now-card per active point, removes numbered cards for points that left active work, and creates a visible stub for an active point that has no card yet so unwritten prose is explicit rather than silently absent.

Reconciliation preserves existing authored now-card prose and markup byte-for-byte for unchanged fields, refuses any mutation that would blank or conflict with existing prose, and changes authored text only through explicit operator input.

While any active points exist, the now-section must match that exact numbered set; an empty section or a partial one blocks with named `missing` points, and an extra stale card blocks with named `extra` points.

A verified zero-point active record renders a parser-distinct non-card empty-state element meaning that no point is demonstrably active; malformed, unreadable or unverifiable source data never renders that empty state and never clears the last authored board.

Point 700’s open clause is resolved by never substituting an unnumbered handover card for active work: transfer, adoption and handover continuity keep numbered now-cards for their points, and only the verified-zero state is unnumbered via the dedicated empty-state element.
The Stop-hook wrapper for the now-section completeness check stands down for `heldByOtherLiveOwner` and `.claude/batch-paused`, keeps the decision logic pure, and fails open on its own error path.
Guard-core tests must pin the measured `[700,697,711]` cases where a sole 700 card and an empty now-section both block and report the missing active points.
Board-core tests must pin that reconciliation creates missing stubs without touching surviving prose, refuses blanking existing prose, and removes cards for points no longer in flight.
Tests must keep the ownership and pause stand-downs, plus the now-section edge cases, covered at the board-core layer.
This point is critical because the user-facing board section that answers whether the batch is running omitted two of three active strands and therefore communicated the opposite of the truth.
The change lands as a combined board/render/guard mechanism change and therefore requires the other model’s recorded review before merge.

The in-flight core must normalize active work as numbered strands from the owner’s structured declaration, deduplicating repeated evidence for one point and treating explicit continuation phases as still active.

Transfer, adoption, session compaction, counter-review and handover are continuity states rather than exits, so their numbered cards remain in the now-section until an explicit lifecycle transition moves them elsewhere.
Reconciliation operates by moving existing numbered card markup between sections and refuses missing-copy or conflicting-copy situations rather than synthesizing new authored prose.

The derived now-section order is deterministic and idempotent: surviving cards keep their relative order, newly inserted cards follow a structured active-work order with point number as tie-break, and repeated reconciliation produces byte-identical output.

Publication performs the exact-set check against the normalized active record and refuses missing, extra, duplicate, unknown or cross-section numbered points; reconcile-and-publish runs as one serialized board operation and a failed publish remains a named non-zero obligation.

The owner’s Stop-hook mismatch check uses the same pure active-set comparison and reports missing/extra numbered points, while publish preflight is intentionally fail-closed because no publication is safer than publishing a knowingly false board.

Guard-core tests must cover duplicate now-cards for one point, cross-section duplication, a nonempty active record against an otherwise empty board, and the removal of the old ‘no board means skip’ escape for a known active-set mismatch.

Batch-in-flight-core tests must cover normalization of repeated evidence to one active point, focus-plus-strand aggregation, exclusion of undeclared open branches, and fail-open handling of malformed or contradictory active-work source data.
Board-core tests must cover lifecycle moves across sections, retention of numbered cards through transfer/adoption continuity, and the verified zero-active-points empty-state element.

The composed tests must prove total fail-open Stop behavior on unreadable source data, fail-closed publish preflight, preserved stand-downs for paused/non-owner states, and continued compatibility with existing topic, done-claim, queue-order and ETA rules.

Point-700 regression coverage must start continuity and handover cases from a numbered active card and separately prove that the verified-zero empty state is parser-distinct and needs no fictitious card to move.
The active-set omission is CRITICAL because it affected a published control surface the user relies on to judge whether autonomous work is running at all.

The point bundles the board-core lifecycle change, dashboard-integrity exact-set enforcement and batch-in-flight active-point normalization because splitting them would preserve either the duplicate-card failure or the incomplete active-work source.
